title: Permissions Reference
summary: Single reference for permission keys, effective access behavior, and role fallback logic.
coverage: How permission checks impact UI and APIs

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Permission checks are enforced on both frontend visibility and backend routes. UI access alone never guarantees API authorization.

sections.title: Authorization model
paragraphs: RAPTOR computes effective permissions from three inputs: role defaults, optional permissions stored for the user, and admin full-access behavior. The backend is authoritative. Most session APIs use `@permission_required(...)`, but that decorator is not the only gate: scanner SSE, collector agent routes, documentation content, admin-only controls, and service-API keys use other checks.
For non-admin users, optional permissions are sanitized against a role-specific allowlist before storage and when evaluated. Invalid or unknown permission values are ignored.

sections.title: Optional permission extensions
paragraphs: Only `user` and `pentester` roles support optional permission extensions. Manager and admin roles do not accept optional extensions. Unknown keys and keys outside each role allowlist are ignored.
Changing role through user administration resets stored optional permissions to an empty set. Optional grants must be explicitly reapplied after role transition when needed.

For `user`, `view_security_dashboard` opens the pentest board only. It does not grant host notebooks (`view_pentest_page`), scan-live, or `/apps/:id`. Neither role can receive `create_manual_records` or `delete_records` as an optional grant.

sections.title: Route and endpoint enforcement patterns
paragraphs: Most session APIs use `@permission_required(...)`. That decorator is not universal. Sensitive admin flows use `@admin_required`. Scanner live streams, collector agents, and documentation pages use other gates described below.

rows: Taxonomy management endpoint, not available to basic users.
Category writes are explicitly separated from category reads.

SSE is not `@permission_required` alone. Viewer is not a sufficient scan-stream role; owner, collaborator, or override is required.
Agent enroll, heartbeat, and ingest authenticate with collector credentials, not session permission keys.

Documentation is filtered by role and permission rules in the docs manifest. It is not an unfiltered dump of every article.

sections.title: Record-level pentest access constraints
paragraphs: Permission keys are not enough. RAPTOR also assigns a record access role: owner (`tested_by`), collaborator, manager or admin override (`modify_others_pentests_admin`), or viewer.

Writes (lifecycle, notes, images, reports) on a host notebook require owner, collaborator, or override. GET host notebooks and Phase 2 finding reads/writes allow that assignment set or environment ACL visibility for the host's environment. Empty env ACL is open; a viewer who is not assigned and is outside a non-empty ACL is denied. Collaborators are a first-class role and can work findings and reports without being `tested_by`.

Environment ACL is a second boundary on Phase 2 finding reads/writes, host search, waves, and report generation for requested env ids. An empty ACL is open to anyone who already has the relevant pentest permission. A non-empty ACL limits access to listed usernames plus `app_lead` and admin/manager override.
